$comment: Play-prototype requests on the app's local socket, beside app-socket.v1 (active), v2 (onboarding), v3 (work), v4 (open) and v5 (handoff), which are unchanged. A separate v rather than a v4 field: an older app answers v6 with its v1 bad_request, which the CLI already reads as app_protocol_mismatch, and v4's readiness and refusal rules stay unmixed. The reader dispatches on numeric v before validating. Use the $defs; the root constrains nothing. The reply says what the app decided, not what the CLI prints: the CLI builds its own messages and next steps from the code.

token.$comment: Not pattern-checked so a wrong token reaches the app's bad_token answer instead of bad_request.

absolutePath.$comment: Absolute POSIX path; the app is macOS-only. Registration is checked by the app.

path.$comment: Repo-relative, '/'-separated canvas path, the same pattern as v4; the app checks the pattern again and then the canvas list.

frame.$comment: The schema bound is 200 code points, while the app and the injected prototype script cap frame ids at 200 UTF-16 units. The CLI refuses an id over 200 UTF-16 units before sending, so an id that passes here can still be one the CLI never sends.

mark.$comment: The frame's raw data-doan-prototype value, which the CLI already judged; the grammar is ARCHITECTURE convention 14, the same literal Go and the app carry, pinned by schema/fixtures/prototype-mark/cases.json.

errorCode.$comment: In the app's check order after the schema and token: project_not_open, not_ready (launch restore or the project still loading, the one retryable answer), busy (first run or the buddy screen; unlike v4, the main window's locked pages and dialogs do not block, because the prototype window moves apart from it), canvas_not_found (not in the canvas list, or its canvas id is shared by two rows). Whether the frame exists and is marked is the CLI's judgment, not a reply code.
